title: Extra shifts on rest days
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in cardiology. A locum agency offers you well-paid twelve-hour shifts at another hospital on your next two rest days, which come straight after a week of long day shifts.

Taking them would put you well over the 72-hour limit in a seven-day period set by your contract, and your contract requires you to tell your employer about any other work. You could do with the money.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Accept just one of the two shifts, to reduce the impact.
options.brief: Still breaches the limit, though by less.
options.detailed: This feels like a compromise, but if one shift still takes you over the limit, you would still be working while fatigued, and against your contract.

options.text: Accept both shifts, and don't tell your employer, as they are at another hospital.
options.detailed: Working at another hospital doesn't change the effect on your fatigue, and not declaring it breaches your contract. This is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Accept both shifts, and tell your employer about them afterwards.
options.brief: Breaches the limit, even though you'd be open about it.
options.detailed: Being open is better than hiding the work, but declaring it afterwards doesn't make it safe. You would still be working beyond the limit.

options.text: Decline the shifts, as they would take you over the safe working limit.
options.brief: Working limits exist to protect patients and you.
options.detailed: The 72-hour limit is there because fatigue causes errors. Working twelve-hour shifts straight after a week of long days would leave you, and your patients, at risk. Declining is the safe choice, however useful the money.

options.text: Look for locum shifts that fit within your limits, and tell your employer about them.
options.brief: Allows you to earn extra safely and openly.
options.detailed: Additional work is allowed when it fits within the limits and is declared. Looking for shifts that do fit is a reasonable way of meeting your financial needs. It ranks second because the decision about these particular shifts comes first.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you put patient safety and honesty with your employer ahead of financial gain.
explanation.keyDetails: The shifts would breach the 72-hour limit and follow a week of long days. Your contract requires you to declare other work. You need the money.
explanation.reasoning: [D] protects patients and you, and [E] finds a safe, open alternative. [A], [C] and [B] all breach the limit, with [B] adding dishonesty.
explanation.competing: The order of [A] and [C] reflects the size of the breach: one shift is less unsafe than two, even though both are wrong.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, making sure your health and fatigue don't put patients at risk; Domain 4, honesty with employers.
